record.paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
record.original_question: For an Enriques surface X with a semiorthogonal decomposition whose residual admissible category is the Kuznetsov component Ku(X,L) determined by an exceptional collection L of line bundles, can the Serre functor of Ku(X,L) be described explicitly and computably, is Ku(X,L) indecomposable, and do the Fourier-Mukai representability questions for exact fully faithful functors or equivalences between admissible subcategories have positive answers for such Kuznetsov components?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $\mathcal{L}=(L_1,\dots,L_n)$ be an exceptional collection of line bundles on $X$ in the bounded derived category $D^b(X)$. Consider the semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X)=\langle \mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L}),\, L_1,\dots,L_nangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ is defined as the right orthogonal to $\langle L_1,\dots,L_nangle$ and is an admissible triangulated subcategory. Address the following:

(a) Give an explicit, computable description of the Serre functor $S_{\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})}$ of $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ (in particular, identify its action on objects up to a shift, and determine whether $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ is a fractional Calabi–Yau or Enriques-type category).

(b) Determine whether $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ is indecomposable as a triangulated category, i.e., admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition.

(c) Decide whether every exact fully faithful functor (respectively, every exact equivalence) between admissible subcategories of the form $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ and $\mathrm{Ku}(X',\mathcal{L}')$ for Enriques surfaces $X,X'$ is of Fourier–Mukai type, i.e., is isomorphic to the restriction of an integral functor with kernel in $D^b(X	imes X')$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists. Refined derived Torelli theorems for Enriques surfaces (Li–Nuer–Stellari and follow-ups) show that for general and then non-generic Enriques surfaces, equivalence of Kuznetsov components implies isomorphism, with Fourier–Mukai type equivalences playing a key role. Structural questions about the Serre functor and indecomposability of Ku(X,L) for general exceptional collections of line bundles, and full Fourier–Mukai representability of fully faithful functors between them, remain not fully resolved in general.

status_evidence.title: A refined derived Torelli theorem for Enriques surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Two general Enriques surfaces are isomorphic if their Kuznetsov components are equivalent.
status_evidence.claim: Categorical Torelli for general Enriques surfaces is established.

status_evidence.title: A refined derived Torelli theorem for Enriques surfaces, II: the non-generic case
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the equivalence-of-Kuznetsov-components-implies-isomorphism result to non-generic Enriques surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on equivalences between Enriques Kuznetsov components.

status_evidence.title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing the question on Serre functor description, indecomposability, and Fourier-Mukai representability for Ku(X,L) as open.
status_evidence.claim: The triple question is explicitly raised as an open problem.
